subject: SIAQ
body: The Private Security Industry Act 2001
options: made searches compulsory at every venue
set up the SIA and made licensing compulsory for door supervisors
explanation: Working without a licence is a criminal offence.

subject: SIAQ
body: While working, a door supervisor must
options: hand it to the venue manager
keep the licence at home for safety
show it only if a customer asks
wear their SIA licence where it can be clearly seen
explanation: Unless the licence conditions say otherwise.

subject: SIAQ
body: A front-line SIA licence normally lasts
explanation: You must renew it before it expires.

subject: SIAQ
body: The four licensing objectives in the Licensing Act 2003 are crime and disorder prevention, public safety, prevention of public nuisance and
explanation: Door supervisors help venues meet these objectives.

subject: SIAQ
body: Selling alcohol to a person who is drunk is
options: an offence under the Licensing Act 2003
explanation: Staff may also refuse entry to drunk people.

subject: SIAQ
body: Under 'Challenge 25', staff should ask for ID from
explanation: Acceptable ID includes a passport, photocard driving licence or PASS-hologram card.

subject: SIAQ
body: Which is an acceptable proof of age?
options: a card with the PASS hologram
a student union membership card without a hologram
a photo of an ID on a phone
a bank card with a name
explanation: Check that the photo and date of birth match.

subject: SIAQ
body: Any force used by a door supervisor must be
explanation: Using excessive force can be a criminal offence.

subject: SIAQ
body: Physical intervention should be used
options: only as a last resort when other options have failed or aren't possible
as a first response to arguments
explanation: Non-physical methods such as communication come first.

subject: SIAQ
body: An 'any person' arrest (citizen's arrest) can be made for
options: an indictable offence, when it is necessary and a police officer cannot make it
any minor rule broken in the venue
explanation: Hand the person to the police as soon as possible.

subject: SIAQ
body: After making an arrest, the door supervisor must
options: keep them in a back room until closing
hand the person over to the police as soon as possible
explanation: Record everything that happened.

subject: SIAQ
body: A customer can only be searched by a door supervisor
options: only if the police are present
with their consent, as a condition of entry
explanation: If they refuse, you can refuse entry.

subject: SIAQ
body: Where possible, a search should be carried out by
options: a member of staff of the same sex as the customer
explanation: Search in view of CCTV and a witness.

subject: SIAQ
body: If you find illegal drugs during a search, you should
options: give them back to the customer
seize them, record the find and hand them to the police
explanation: Follow the venue's drugs policy.

subject: SIAQ
body: Positional asymmetry means standing
options: at an angle to the person, not square-on
explanation: It looks less confrontational and keeps you safer.

subject: SIAQ
body: A good way to calm an angry customer is to
options: listen, stay calm and explain the reasons for decisions
explanation: Empathy helps de-escalate conflict.

subject: SIAQ
body: In the attitude and behaviour cycle,
options: staff behaviour can never change outcomes
your attitude affects your behaviour, which affects theirs
explanation: Staying positive helps prevent escalation.

subject: SIAQ
body: Which body language is most likely to escalate conflict?
explanation: Non-verbal signals matter as much as words.

subject: SIAQ
body: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, 'Charlie Delta' stands for
explanation: It avoids confusion over radios.

subject: SIAQ
body: Radio messages should be
options: short, clear and to the point
explanation: Wait for a gap before speaking.

subject: SIAQ
body: Someone who appears very drunk and alone outside the venue is
options: potentially vulnerable and needs your help to stay safe
explanation: Consider safe places, friends, taxis or emergency services.

subject: SIAQ
body: If you suspect a customer's drink has been spiked, you should
options: give them more water and leave them
send them home alone in a taxi
keep them with a trusted person, get medical help and inform police
explanation: Keep the drink as evidence if possible.

subject: SIAQ
body: A sign of child sexual exploitation could be
options: a young person with older adults who control their movements
a group of friends celebrating a birthday
explanation: Report concerns following the venue's safeguarding procedure.

subject: SIAQ
body: The HOT principle for suspicious items asks if an item is Hidden, Obviously suspicious and
options: Typical of what you'd expect in that place
explanation: If it's suspicious, don't touch it.

subject: SIAQ
body: The 4 Cs for a suspicious item are Confirm, Clear, Communicate and
explanation: Keep people away from the area.

subject: SIAQ
body: In a weapons or firearms attack, the public advice is
explanation: Run if safe, hide if you can't, and tell police by calling 999.

subject: SIAQ
body: Hostile reconnaissance means
options: someone gathering information to plan an attack
explanation: Report unusual interest in security measures.

subject: SIAQ
body: On hearing the fire alarm, a door supervisor should
options: use the lift to clear upper floors
keep people inside until the music stops
follow the evacuation plan and guide people to the exits
explanation: Report to the assembly point and help account for people.

subject: SIAQ
body: Fire exits must be kept
options: clear and unlocked while the venue is open
locked to stop people sneaking in
explanation: Blocked exits cost lives.

subject: SIAQ
body: A sign that a crowd may be becoming dangerous is
options: people being pushed and unable to move freely
people leaving through the exits calmly
explanation: Act early to reduce density.

subject: SIAQ
body: The Equality Act 2010 lists how many protected characteristics?
explanation: They include age, disability, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

subject: SIAQ
body: Refusing entry because of a person's race is
options: allowed if the manager says so
explanation: Entry decisions must be fair and consistent.

subject: SIAQ
body: An incident report should be
options: written a week later from memory
written as soon as possible, factually and accurately
left out if nobody was hurt
explanation: It may be used as evidence in court.

subject: SIAQ
body: CCTV images of people are personal data, so they must be
options: handled under the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018
explanation: Only authorised people should access them.

subject: SIAQ
body: When ejecting a customer, door supervisors should
options: eject them through the busiest exit
explain the reason, give them the chance to leave and use force only if necessary
keep their coat as a penalty
explanation: Make sure they're safe once outside.

subject: SIAQ
body: Door supervisors who work alone outside should
options: leave their post without telling anyone
switch radios off to save batteries
keep regular contact with colleagues by radio
explanation: Lone working increases risk.

subject: SIAQ
body: Which is a common sign that a person may have taken drugs?
explanation: Signs vary; treat it as a welfare concern too.

subject: SIAQ
body: A licensed venue's Designated Premises Supervisor (DPS) is
options: the named person with day-to-day responsibility for selling alcohol
explanation: Door supervisors work with the DPS and venue management.

subject: SIAQ
body: If a customer is injured during a physical intervention, you should
options: get first aid, record the incident and report it to your supervisor
say nothing in case of trouble
tell them to see their GP next week
explanation: Accurate records protect everyone.

subject: SIAQ
body: If a customer refuses a search that is a condition of entry, you should
options: let them in without a search
call the police to force a search
explanation: Explain the venue's policy calmly.
